Kenley
England
57Secondary Students
Established in 2015 and located 12 miles outside central London in Surrey’s leafy suburbs, OneSchool Global Kenley Campus occupies a Grade II listed building near the historical Kenley Aerodrome, a significant Battle of Britain site. Our 103 students and 23 staff members enjoy this thoughtfully restored facility that blends architectural heritage with modern educational needs.
Since inception, the campus has pursued a program of continual development and improvement, resulting in a well-proven centre of educational achievement. Students at all levels are supported by our qualified and passionate teaching staff who share a collective enthusiasm for learning.
We expect a high level of commitment by students, and the full support of our parents is an essential ingredient to success.

pageCache.text:
Kenley teacher wins prestigious silver teaching award
SHARE
Abbey Tune, geography lead based at our Kenley campus in the UK, has been recognised in two prestigious education awards.
She has been awarded a Silver 2026 Pearson National Teaching Award for ‘Teacher of the Year in a Secondary School’ and was recognised as a finalist in the TES School Awards for ‘Subject Lead of the Year (Secondary)’.
The Pearson awards celebrate outstanding teachers and education professionals across the UK. Abbey learned she had received the award as part of ‘National Thank a Teacher Day’ on 17 June 2026.
Staff and students at OneSchool Global (OSG) Kenley marked the achievement with a morning tea celebration at the school, where Abbey also received her Silver prize.
Commenting on the award win, Abbey said: “I am honoured to have been named a Silver winner in the Pearson Education Awards, Secondary School Teacher of the Year category, and as a finalist in the TES School Awards. That said, I already feel like a winner every day in my role.
“I am fortunate to work in a job I genuinely love, supported by fantastic pupils, dedicated staff, and a strong, caring community. The Learning to Learn framework embodies everything I value about education, and it has allowed me to teach in the way I have always aspired to; focusing on independence, curiosity, and meaningful growth.
“I am truly grateful for all the support I have received throughout this journey, on campus by staff and leadership, and am thrilled to secure Silver while representing OSG Kenley Campus.”
Abbey will now be recognised at The Pearson National Teaching Awards UK Ceremony, which will be held in London in late November 2026.
She will also learn at the ceremony whether she has been named a Gold winner.
About OneSchool Global OneSchool Global is an independent school network that has more than 8,000 primary and secondary students and 2,000 staff across the globe, in regions including United Kingdom, North America, Europe, Australia, Argentina, New Zealand and the Caribbean. Our students come from the Plymouth Brethren Christian Church community; however, OneSchool Global is not a religious school and only teaches religion as required in the curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: OneSchool Global Kenley students raise £2,820 for Teenage Cancer Trust - One School Global
pageCache.text:
OneSchool Global Kenley students raise £2,820 for Teenage Cancer Trust
Students
Fundraising
SHARE
Students at OneSchool Global’s Kenley campus have raised £2,820 for Teenage Cancer Trust, smashing their original £250 target through a 14-mile sponsored walk.
The initiative began near the end of the summer term as part of GCSE Citizenship exam preparation. Year 9 students were asked to research a charity, explore its impact locally and nationally, and create a campaign to raise awareness and funds. After debate and discussion, the group chose Teenage Cancer Trust for its vital work supporting young people with cancer.
What started as a modest goal quickly grew. Within weeks, the team exceeded their target, and five months later, they had walked 14.13 miles and raised more than ten times their original ambition. Their success reflects not only teamwork and commitment but also the Learning to Learn framework in action – applying research, planning, and collaboration skills to answer a real-world question.
Student Daniel explained, “We chose to raise funds because each member of the team has known someone that has suffered from cancer. Even though those people weren’t necessarily teenagers at the time, we are all teenagers now and know that we have every possibility of suffering from the disease later in our lives.”
Teacher Craig Hunter praised the effort: “This started with a small idea to answer a big question. The boys grew it into something far beyond what we imagined.”
Julia Bennett from Teenage Cancer Trust visited our Kenley campus to receive the donation and thank the students for their contribution. She said:
“Their compassion, energy and teamwork show the incredible power of young people coming together to make a difference.”
The success has inspired more charitable projects at Kenley, including a Year 10 campaign for Guide Dogs for the Blind and plans for a campus-wide Teenage Cancer Trust initiative.
